expenditures.detail: The 13 written Schedule B rows sum to 18.18 + 128.81 + 75.22 + 545.90 + 83.66 + 16.11 + 143.12 + 7.51 + 45.91 + 26.74 + 1.51 + 35.06 + 94.94 = 1,222.67 exactly = the page subtotal = the sum-of-all-pages total = the promoted per-period Box D. Box E (YTD) prints the identical figure. ⚠ THIS CLOSURE WAS NOT FREE, AND THE PROCESS IS THE POINT: read at 200 dpi the rows summed to 1,222.63, a 0.04 shortfall. Before calling that a filer-arithmetic delta the ADDENDUM H3 screen was run — every band was cropped and checked for a DOUBLED band holding two entries — and it came back clean; the ADDENDUM F1 screen for a row written below the last printed rule was run too (the band-14 control rendered an empty cell). Then ALL THIRTEEN amount cells were escalated to tight 700-1200 dpi crops, and two were misreads of the low-contrast phone capture, not the filer's arithmetic: row 6 is 16.11 (not 16.1 — a second thin 1 in the cents) and row 10 is 26.74 (not 26.71 — the filer's two-stroke 4). +0.01 and +0.03 exactly account for the shortfall and the side closes to the cent. NOTHING WAS NUDGED to make it close: each corrected cell was read at resolution first and the arithmetic then confirmed the reading, which is the order GOTCHAS requires. The other eleven cells reproduced their 200 dpi values exactly.

in_kind_convention: monetary-only — and the two conventions are identical here. This filing's Schedule A prints FOUR columns (Date / Name of Contributor / Address and Zip Code / Amount) with NO in-kind checkbox column, no row on either schedule is annotated in-kind, and the Summary Page carries no in-kind line and no compound '+Inkind' cell. Both conventions give 1,222.67 on each side and both close exactly.
escalation_note: Twenty-two crops, all named with this filing's key — by far the most in this chunk, because the document is a PHONE CAMERA CAPTURE ('Made with Scanner App' watermark on every page) with a hand shadow falling across the left half of pp2-3, and rowbands.py returns ZERO printed rules on every page at 200 dpi. (1) GEOMETRY had to be measured from scratch: a background-normalised dark-run scan of the render (subtract a 25 px Gaussian blur, then threshold) recovered the printed grid where the tool's fixed threshold could not — p2 columns at 8.13 / 20.85 / 49.65 / 77.15 / 90.57 and p3 at 7.43 / 20.28 / 49.64 / 77.52 / 90.81, with the row rules found inside the AMOUNT column alone, which is the best-lit part of both photographs. On p2 the shadow swallowed the rules above 39%, so the top five bands were extrapolated backwards at the measured 4.25 pitch and then CROP-PROVED. (2) ALL THIRTEEN p3 amount cells were escalated to 700-1200 dpi to settle a 0.04 shortfall; two were corrected (16.1 -> 16.11, 26.71 -> 26.74) and eleven reproduced exactly, after which the side closes to the cent — see recon.expenditures.detail for the full order of operations. (3) THE DATE COLUMNS of both schedules were cropped at 700 dpi: this filer's 6 is a small closed loop with a lead-in stroke and his 4 is a two-stroke printed 4, and the two forms appear together in one cell on p3 row 13 ('4/16/26'), so every year on this filing reads /26 and none reads /20 or /24. On p2 row 1 the year glyph is traced over twice in heavier ink; it is still a 6.

Schedule A is a boxed 15-row grid. rowbands.py returns ZERO rules here; the grid was recovered by a background-normalised dark-run scan of the 100 dpi render (see escalation_note), which gave column rules at 8.13 / 20.85 / 49.65 / 77.15 / 90.57 and, inside the amount column, row rules from 39.49 downwards on a 4.25 pitch. THE HAND SHADOW ACROSS THE UPPER LEFT SWALLOWED THE RULES ABOVE 39%, so the first five bands were extrapolated backwards at that pitch to a grid top of 18.24 — and then proved, which is what makes them a measurement rather than a guess. TWO-CROP PROOF at 900 dpi: pct:77.09,18.24,13.5,4.25@p2 rendered '$100.00' with the printed 'Amount' header directly above it (recorded 100.00, and the header proves no row was lost above band 1); pct:77.09,26.74,13.5,4.25@p2 rendered '$1022.67' (recorded 1022.67, the last written row). ONE-PAST-THE-END CONTROL pct:77.09,30.99,13.5,4.25@p2 rendered a WHOLLY EMPTY ruled cell. A third crop at pct:77.09,22.49,13.5,4.25@p2 rendered '$100.00' for row 2. ⚠ WORTH RECORDING: on this filing the AMOUNT sits noticeably HIGHER inside its cell than the date and name written on the same row — the date/name text drifts down toward, and on row 3 across, the rule below it, the ADDENDUM J1/N1 hazard. Geometry is anchored on the AMOUNT column, where every value falls squarely inside its own band, so the indexing is unaffected; but a reader who anchored on the date column here would be off by one on row 3.

contributions.note: THE ADDRESS CELL HOLDS A BARE DASH ('-') and nothing else — the filer's own explicit nil mark, not an untouched cell and not a county redaction (this page carries no redaction bars). Under the repo-wide zero-glyph ruling a bare dash is a NIL MARK, not a value, so donor_city and donor_state are honestly BLANK; the dash is quoted here rather than transcribed into a field. This is a distinct blank-address cause from the ones the wave has catalogued so far (redacted by the county / left empty by the filer / the form prints a zip and no city / lost in reproduction / city and zip but no state / no address field exists / the cell holds a payment channel / 'Anonymous'): here the filer AFFIRMATIVELY MARKED the cell nil. The year glyph is traced over twice in heavier ink and reads 26, matching this filer's loop-6 elsewhere on the filing.
Address cell holds a BARE DASH, same as row 1 — the filer's explicit nil mark; donor_city and donor_state honestly blank, nothing redacted on this page.

notes: FORM CHARACTERISATION (2026 stock, eighth specimen) — variant modern_boxAF, masthead 'Aaron Davidson, Clerk', four pages, summary LAST, each page classified from its own printed header: p1 cover, p2 'Schedule A - Itemized Contributions Received', p3 'Schedule B - Itemized Expenditures Made', p4 'Summary Page'. NN.NN' string can be read off the page and none is asserted (index.csv's form_version is empty for this filing, consistent with that). The blank is nonetheless identifiable by its columns, and it is the 'Address and Zip Code' Schedule A — the same blank Brian Voeks used (a9fc51aa) and NOT the 'City and Zip Code' blank Bowles, Herrin, Forbush, Evans and Tribe used. Schedule B carries the real Purpose column (Date / Provider/Vendor / Purpose / Amount); both schedules are boxed 15-row grids printing their own two footers; the Summary Page prints A, B/C, D/E, F and an UNLETTERED close box. Report type '30 Days after withdrawal or elimination' is ticked, the amendment question is ticked 'No', the report is dated 04/24/2026 throughout, and foliation is continuous counting the cover and complete ('1 of 4' ... '4 of 4'), which agrees with pdfinfo's page count — a rare case in this corpus where the filer's own foliation confirms the document is whole. HYBRID FILL: the identity block, the candidate-name boxes, the Date of Report boxes, Box A and the close box are TYPED into the fillable PDF, while every schedule row and Boxes B through F are HANDWRITTEN. ** THE DOCUMENT IS A PHONE CAMERA CAPTURE, NOT A SCAN ** — a 'Made with Scanner App' watermark sits at the foot of every page, each page has a different oversized mediabox, and a hand shadow falls across the left half of pp2-3. Two consequences a later reader should know: rowbands.py returns ZERO printed rules on all four pages so the geometry had to be measured by a background-normalised scan (see the measure_notes), and the low contrast cost two cents-digit misreads at 200 dpi that only tight escalation recovered (16.1 -> 16.11, 26.71 -> 26.74). Both were caught by the page's own arithmetic and corrected AT RESOLUTION, not nudged. PAGE-FACE IDENTITY: the cover, the affirmation line and every sheet's candidate box read 'Richard Smith', while index.csv's channel label is 'Richard Neal Smith' — the middle name is a channel artifact and does not appear on the page. The OFFICE BOX reads 'County Commission' typed with 'Seat A' added by hand, corroborating index.csv's 'County Commission Seat A' from the page itself. REDACTION — the third instance in this chunk of a '_Redacted' filing that publishes the candidate's own address: the county blacked out the cover's phone-and-email block and the signature block, and left the full home street address, city, state and zip in the clear. Neither schedule carries any redaction at all, which is why the two dash-marked donor address cells on p2 are recorded as THE FILER'S OWN NIL MARK rather than as redactions, and why the one street line printed on p2 row 3 had to be dropped by this transcription rather than by the clerk.
